title: Give the Model a Finger: Developmentally Aligned Evaluation of Counting in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27756v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are exact on small sets and drift into estimation on larger ones, a profile reminiscent of children before they master counting. Children cross the barrier with epistemic actions: pointing at each item while reciting number words, moving counted items aside, partitioning the array. We give VLMs the same actions as dumb image tools with no visual intelligence of their own in a training-free agent loop. Our central claim is about measurement, not intervention: a model that counts by marking leaves a normally hidden serial procedure on the image, and the developmental principles of counting turn those marks into an interpretable audit of serial visual reasoning: every tag is classified against point-level ground truth as on-target, duplicate, phantom, or omitted, the answer is checked against the number of tags, and order irrelevance is tested by forcing opposite traversal orders. translated_title: 给模型一根手指：视觉语言模型计数能力的发展对齐评估
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLM）在小集合上表现精确，而在较大集合上则退化为估计，这一特征与尚未掌握计数的儿童颇为相似。儿童通过认知动作跨越这一障碍：一边念数词一边指向每个物品，把已数过的物品移到一边，或对物品阵列进行分组。我们以无需训练的智能体循环方式，为VLM提供同样的动作——这些动作只是不具备自身视觉智能的“哑”图像工具。我们的核心主张在于测量而非干预：一个通过标记进行计数的模型，会将其通常隐藏的串行过程留在图像上，而计数的发展性原则将这些标记转变为对串行视觉推理的可解释审计：每个标记都会依据点级真值被分类为命中、重复、幻影或遗漏；答案会与标记数量进行核对；顺序无关性则通过强制相反的遍历顺序来检验。在9个模型、682张图像的实验中……
tldr: 该论文受儿童计数发展过程启发，提出一种无需训练的智能体评估框架，让视觉语言模型通过“指认标记”等认知动作进行计数，将模型通常隐藏的串行视觉推理过程转化为可解释、可审计的行为分析。
en_tdlr: Inspired by developmental principles of how children learn counting, this paper introduces a training-free agent evaluation framework where vision-language models count through epistemic marking actions, turning their normally hidden serial visual reasoning into an interpretable and auditable process.
